event: Brussels Airport closed after the attack
evidence: The airport was closed after the bombings in the departure hall on 22 March 2016 and reopened on Sunday 3 April with three flights from a temporary check-in facility.
Dublin Airport stopped operating from 3 pm on 1 March 2018 with all arrivals and departures cancelled until at least the following afternoon; on 3 March most operations began only after 10 am.

event: Gatwick: runway closed after drone sightings
source: CBS News; Wikipedia (Gatwick Airport drone incident)
evidence: Gatwick closed its only runway and suspended all flights after drone sightings; hundreds of flights were cancelled between 19 and 21 December 2018, about 1,000 flights affected.
note: The disruption ran from the evening of 19 December to 21 December; the window of the test is 20 December only.

source: EUROCONTROL daily traffic situation (as republished by ATC Network); Euronews
evidence: On 29 March 2020 network flights were 88.0% below the same day of 2019; by state: Spain -93%, France -93%, United Kingdom -87%, Germany -87%, Netherlands -85%.
note: The evidence is by state and network, not by airport. This is a collapse of traffic, not a closure; it was placed in the closure class before the test and is left there.

source: ch-aviation; EASA conflict zone information (as quoted)
evidence: The Ukrainian air traffic service closed the airspace to all civilian flights by notice from 00:45 UTC on 24 February 2022; EASA declared an active conflict zone.
All 232 departing passenger flights were cancelled on 20 June 2022 because most security staff had walked out; about one in four inbound flights arrived; freight flights were not disrupted.
note: Departures of passenger flights were cancelled; arrivals and freight partly operated. Placed in the closure class before the test and left there.

evidence: A full-day strike on 17 February 2023 at Frankfurt, Munich, Stuttgart, Hamburg, Dortmund, Hanover and Bremen; regular flight operations were suspended for the day at Frankfurt, Munich, Hamburg and Stuttgart; more than 2,300 flights were affected.

source: CNN; Wikipedia (2023 German public transport strike)
evidence: On 27 March 2023 Frankfurt airport had no regular passenger flights; Munich airport had no regular passenger or cargo traffic on 26 and 27 March.
All flights were grounded at Munich Airport on 2 December 2023 after more than 40 cm of snow, until 6 am on Sunday 3 December; 760 flights were affected.

event: Heathrow closed after a power failure
evidence: Heathrow was closed until 23:59 on 21 March 2025 after a fire at the North Hyde electrical substation; at least 1,350 flights were affected.
About 350 flights were cancelled at Schiphol on 18 February 2022 in storm Eunice, more than 200 of them by KLM; the airport said a full stop of air traffic was not necessary.

source: UK Civil Aviation Authority (independent review); International Airport Review
evidence: The flight planning system at Swanwick failed on 28 August 2023; 799 departures and 786 arrivals at UK airports were cancelled that day (about 27% of each), most at Heathrow, then Gatwick.
Frankfurt Airport was closed to departing passengers on 7 March 2024 during strikes of security staff and of Lufthansa ground staff; about 650 of 1,170 scheduled flights were cancelled.

event_type: IT outage; cancellations and a suspension
evidence: On 19 July 2024 about 200 flights were cancelled at Schiphol and every flight was delayed or cancelled; Berlin Brandenburg halted all flights until 10 am.

source: AirNav Radar; The New York Sun (Associated Press)
evidence: On 28 April 2025 the grid of Spain and Portugal collapsed at about 12:30; Madrid Barajas and Lisbon airports lost power and Lisbon accepted no arrivals for a time.
